skill.name: verification-before-completion
skill.description: Require fresh verification evidence before claiming work is complete, fixed, passing, or ready to ship.
skill.summary: Guides agents to run and inspect verification before making completion claims.

content.value_statement: AI agents can overstate progress when they rely on assumptions instead of fresh evidence. This skill enforces a clear verification gate before completion, fix, or passing claims.
actual_capabilities: Requires fresh verification before claims about passing tests, successful builds, or completed work.
Defines a five-step gate for identifying, running, reading, and confirming verification output.
Lists common false shortcuts, such as relying on prior runs or partial checks.
Provides examples for tests, builds, requirements, regression tests, and delegated agent work.
Encourages honest status reporting when verification fails or remains incomplete.
limitations: Does not provide project-specific test or build commands.
Does not automate verification by itself; the agent must run the relevant tools.
Cannot prove correctness beyond the verification commands selected for the task.
May increase task time when full verification is slow.

use_cases.title: Prevent premature completion claims
use_cases.description: Require an agent to run the relevant command before saying a task is done or fixed.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers using AI coding assistants

use_cases.title: Improve review readiness
use_cases.description: Create a habit of checking tests, builds, and requirements before commits or pull requests.

use_cases.title: Verify delegated agent work
use_cases.description: Check diffs and run verification instead of accepting another agent's success report at face value.

prompt_templates.title: Basic verification check
prompt_templates.prompt: Before you say this is complete, identify the command that proves it, run it, read the output, and report the actual result.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after a small bug fix or simple code change.

prompt_templates.title: Build and test confirmation
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify this change with the relevant test and build commands. Only claim success if the fresh output confirms it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before committing or opening a pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Requirement checklist verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Re-read the requirements, create a checklist, verify each item with evidence, and report any gaps without assuming completion.

prompt_templates.title: Delegated work audit
prompt_templates.prompt: An agent reported success. Inspect the diff, verify the intended behavior, run the necessary checks, and report the true status with evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when another assistant or subagent completed part of the work.

output_examples.input: I changed the parser. Can I say the bug is fixed?
output_examples.output: Not yet. Run the regression test that reproduces the parser bug, inspect the output, and only then state whether it is fixed.

output_examples.input: The linter passed, so is the build good?
output_examples.output: No. A passing linter does not prove compilation. Run the build command and report its exit status and relevant output.

output_examples.input: The subagent says it finished the refactor.
output_examples.output: Verify independently. Review the VCS diff, run the relevant checks, and report the actual state rather than trusting the success message.

best_practices: Choose the verification command that directly proves the claim you want to make.
Read the full command output and check the exit code before summarizing results.
Report uncertainty or failures clearly instead of converting them into success claims.
anti_patterns: Saying work should pass because the code looks correct.
Using a partial check as proof for a broader claim.
Trusting an agent success report without checking the diff and behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It tells the agent to identify and run the correct verification commands for the current project.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it before any claim that work is complete, fixed, passing, ready to commit, or ready for review.

faq.question: Does a passing linter prove the build works?
faq.answer: No. The skill treats linting, testing, building, and behavior checks as separate forms of evidence.

faq.question: Can prior test output count as evidence?
faq.answer: No. The skill requires fresh verification in the current context before making a success claim.

faq.question: How does it help with delegated agent work?
faq.answer: It requires checking the actual diff and running verification instead of relying on another agent's summary.

faq.question: Is this skill useful outside Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow applies to Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when they perform software tasks.
